intro.title: React Server Components & SSR vs SSG
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that demonstrates the concepts of server-side rendering (SSR) and static site generation (SSG) to understand how they differ from client-side rendering. You'll learn how to pre-render content on the server for faster initial page loads and better SEO, similar to React's SSR and SSG approaches. The core programming concept involves configuring Vue's build tools to generate static HTML or use a Node.js server for on-demand rendering. You'll work with Vue components, build configurations, and basic server concepts, all within a beginner-friendly Vue context.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building high-performance, content-heavy applications like e-commerce product pages, news websites, and social media feeds. For example, an e-commerce site uses Server-Side Rendering (SSR) to ensure product listings and details are immediately visible for SEO and fast initial load, while interactive elements like shopping cart buttons are handled client-side. Static Site Generation (SSG) is perfect for marketing pages, blogs, or documentation where content changes infrequently, enabling lightning-fast delivery from a CDN. Understanding when to use each approach allows developers to optimize performance and user experience in real-world projects like dashboards that blend static data panels with dynamic, user-specific widgets.
